subject.title: [Bug]: Agents should not be able to access or modify files outside their own working space.

question: Should OpenClaw make per-agent workspace confinement a default hard boundary, an opt-in strict mode, or part of the broader filesystem policy tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7722?
rationale: This decision defines a security boundary and compatibility posture for existing users who may intentionally rely on host filesystem access.

options.title: Choose a default-compatible strict boundary
options.body: Keep current trusted-host behavior explicit while adding or enabling a clearly documented strict per-agent boundary with migration and proof.

options.title: Fold into the filesystem policy tracker
options.body: Treat this concrete report as a scenario under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7722 and require allowed/denied path plus exec-scope design before implementation.

options.title: Defer to sandbox backends only
options.body: Document Docker/SSH/OpenShell sandboxing as the supported hard boundary and avoid adding another host filesystem policy surface.

recommendation.title: Choose a default-compatible strict boundary
recommendation.body: Keep current trusted-host behavior explicit while adding or enabling a clearly documented strict per-agent boundary with migration and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history on the optional workspace-only guard, filesystem policy resolver, and current maintainer-side review context.
